security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline file references, CSS border declarations, and JavaScript RegExp.exec(). The confirmed issues are low-severity third-party CDN and Google Fonts loads in the generated artifact template, which create privacy, availability, and supply-chain considerations.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js from cdnjs.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a vetted local copy of p5.js or pin an integrity-checked script with a documented update process.

remediation.issue: The viewer template loads Google Fonts and preconnects to Google font domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use system fonts, bundle local font files, or clearly disclose the external font requests to users.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger noisy command-execution detections.
remediation.suggestion: Consider avoiding backtick-heavy examples or annotate them as non-executable documentation to reduce future scanner noise.

content.value_statement: Creating reproducible algorithmic art usually requires creative direction, p5.js structure, and usable controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce seeded browser artifacts with interactive exploration.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Generates p5.js-based interactive HTML art artifacts.
Uses seeded randomness for reproducible visual variations.
Adds parameter controls for tuning generated artwork.
Supports seed navigation and PNG download behavior in the template.
Provides reusable viewer and generator reference templates.
limitations: Generated artifacts depend on browser execution and p5.js support.
The template loads third-party CDN and font resources unless modified.
Visual quality depends on the prompt and model implementation choices.
It does not produce native image files without running the HTML artifact.

use_cases.title: Prototype Browser Artifacts
use_cases.description: Create a self-contained HTML artwork with sliders, seed controls, and download actions for rapid visual testing.

use_cases.title: Explore Reproducible Variations
use_cases.description: Generate seeded outputs so clients or teams can compare consistent art variations across different prompts.

use_cases.title: Teach Generative Systems
use_cases.description: Use the philosophy-first workflow to explain how noise, particles, fields, and parameters shape computational art.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a generative artwork inspired by wind over grass. Include a short algorithmic philosophy and one interactive HTML artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create seeded p5.js generative art using soft geometric motion, calm colors, and controls for density, scale, speed, and palette.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Variation Explorer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt focused on reproducible exploration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive generative art artifact with seed navigation, parameter sliders, reset behavior, and PNG download support.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Complete Series
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a themed collection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-piece generative art series with one shared philosophy, distinct algorithms, and clear seed recommendations for each piece.

output_examples.input: Create generative art based on tidal memory.
output_examples.output: A concise computational philosophy, followed by an interactive HTML artifact with wave-based motion, seed controls, and adjustable flow parameters.

output_examples.input: Make an Art Blocks style particle field with calm colors.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready p5.js artwork that uses seeded particles, palette controls, density sliders, regeneration, reset, and PNG download.
A seed-driven artifact where each seed produces a stable variation that can be navigated, compared, and exported.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual concept and name the desired mood, motion, and level of complexity.
Ask for seed controls and parameter sliders when you need repeatable exploration.
Review generated HTML before sharing it, especially if external resources must be removed.
anti_patterns: Do not request static image output when you need interactive generative behavior.
Do not ask for many unrelated visual styles in one artifact.
Do not publish generated artifacts without checking external dependencies and browser behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a generative art concept and a self-contained p5.js HTML artifact with interactive controls.

faq.question: Does it create reproducible artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow emphasizes seeded randomness so the same seed can produce the same result.

faq.question: Can users adjust the artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The template supports sliders, color controls, seed navigation, reset, regeneration, and PNG download.

faq.question: Does it require a server?
faq.answer: No. The generated HTML is intended to run directly in a browser or Claude artifact environment.

faq.question: Does it use external resources?
faq.answer: Yes by default. The template loads p5.js from a CDN and fonts from Google unless the author changes it.

faq.question: Who is this best for?
faq.answer: It is best for artists, designers, educators, and creative developers who want interactive algorithmic art.
